page: Hetzner Cloud cpx52 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC processor running under QEMU virtualization. It features 12 vCPUs with shared CPU allocation, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 23.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled locally, consisting of a 480 GB NVMe SSD. There are no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU tests placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core tests, falls within the average range. Memory performance is a notable strength; the instance achieves strong ratings in large-block read (220.5 GB/sec) and write (143.81 GB/sec) bandwidth tests, alongside a strong Passmark memory score. Additionally, the processor supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI, which contribute to strong performance in small-to-medium LLM inference tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the cpx52 offers a high density of vCPUs and NVMe storage relative to its resource tier. However, because the CPU allocation is shared, workloads may experience performance variability compared to dedicated thread instances. The 1.95 GB of RAM per core represents a lower memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it less suitable for memory-intensive databases but highly efficient for compute-bound tasks that do not require dedicated CPU guarantees.

This server is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference. It is also appropriate for general-purpose compute workloads, batch processing, and development environments that benefit from high core counts and fast local NVMe storage without requiring sustained 100% dedicated CPU utilization.
